item.title: Installation
item.description:
CoMLRL can be installed from PyPI, conda-forge, or source. Python 3.10 or later is largely recommended. Users can install a PyTorch build compatible with their device.

Installation from PyPI#

pip install comlrl
# Install PyTorch compatible with your device.

Installation from conda-forge#

conda install -c conda-forge comlrl
# Install PyTorch compatible with your device.

Installation from source#

Users can clone the repository and install CoMLRL in editable mode to access the latest features or develop it locally:

item.title: Model Loading & Saving
item.description:
CoMLRL supports both homogeneous and heterogeneous models from Hugging Face or local directories. Users can specify Hugging Face model identifiers through agent_model/critic_model for homogeneous setups, or provide agents/critics lists for heterogeneous setups. Trained agents can be saved and loaded into a new trainer for further training.

Loading LLM Agents#

Homogeneous Agents#

Users can initialize homogeneous agents by setting agent_model to a single model identifier and leaving agents=None. For trainers with a separate num_agents constructor argument, users can set it alongside the matching configuration value; the configuration alone does not override it.

item.title: Dataset Loading
item.description:
Users can keep task inputs and metadata in the same dataset, with a separate split for evaluation. This guide prepares training and evaluation data for the length-ratio task from the quick start.

Dataset Splits#

Each dataset row is a dictionary. The default formatter reads its prompt field; additional fields can hold targets, labels, test cases, or other information required by the reward function. Trainers pass the original row to the reward function through batch_items.

item.title: Logging Metric
item.description:
CoMLRL supports local evaluation records, training curves in Weights & Biases, and task-specific metrics. The examples use the trainer and held-out split from Dataset Loading.

Local Metrics#

Evaluation returns a metrics dictionary even when W&B is disabled. Users can save this dictionary locally to record a completed evaluation:

import json
from pathlib import Path

# Use the MAGRPO trainer and eval_dataset from the Dataset Loading guide.
metrics = trainer.evaluate(num_eval_samples=len(eval_dataset))
Path("eval-metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2) + "\n")

Weights & Biases#

Users can record training curves in Weights & Biases by supplying wandb_config when creating the trainer:

item.title: Training Parallelization
item.description:
CoMLRL trainers run in a Python process. For IAC, parallel_training="none" is the default; "mp" enables scheduling agents and critics on explicitly assigned devices. Neither mode requires a job scheduler.

Model Parallelization#

Users can configure IACTrainer by passing an IACConfig through its args parameter. The following configuration uses four visible CUDA devices and two agents:

from comlrl.trainers.actor_critic import IACConfig

config = IACConfig(
 num_agents=2,
 num_turns=1,
 use_separate_critic=True,
 parallel_training="mp",
 agent_devices=["cuda:0", "cuda:1"],
 critic_devices=["cuda:2", "cuda:3"],
)

agent_devices is required in "mp" mode. critic_devices is also required when use_separate_critic=True. Each model stays on its assigned device; this does not split an individual model across GPUs. Responses are passed to the reward function, and the rewards are used for each agent’s update.

item.title: Q&A
item.description:
What are the differences between CoMLRL and other multi-LLM training frameworks?

Many approaches train role-conditioned agents with shared parameters using single-agent RL frameworks. Distinct agents better represent heterogeneous LLMs with different capabilities and more directly reflect the multi-agent setting.

CoMLRL supports separate actors with decentralized execution, including training with a centralized critic. Its centralized collaboration mode instead uses one actor to generate the complete joint response. The available trainers include REINFORCE, Actor-Critic, and Multi-Agent Preference Learning; each method’s page describes its implemented objective and constraints.
